questions.prompt: A rocket expels propellant at \(18\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}\) with exhaust speed \(2200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the thrust.
A rocket has \(v_e=2500\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and mass ratio \(m_0/m_f=3.0\). Find the ideal \(\Delta v\).
A deep-space rocket needs \(\Delta v=1800\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) with \(v_e=3000\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the required mass ratio.
A vertical rocket has mass \(1200\,\mathrm{kg}\), thrust \(18000\,\mathrm{N}\), and negligible drag. Find its initial upward acceleration near Earth.
A rocket burns from \(900\,\mathrm{kg}\) to \(600\,\mathrm{kg}\) at mass flow rate \(15\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}\). Find the burn time.
A deep-space rocket has dry final mass \(800\,\mathrm{kg}\), exhaust speed \(2500\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and required \(\Delta v=1500\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the initial mass and propellant mass.
questions.answer:
The mass ratio is
\[
\frac{m_0}{m_f}=e^{1500/2500}=1.822
\]
With \(m_f=800\,\mathrm{kg}\),
\[
m_0=1.822(800)=1458\,\mathrm{kg}
\]
Propellant mass is
\[
1458-800=658\,\mathrm{kg}
\]

questions.prompt: A vertical rocket burns from \(1200\,\mathrm{kg}\) to \(800\,\mathrm{kg}\) in \(20\,\mathrm{s}\) with \(v_e=2500\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Ignoring drag, find the burnout speed from rest including gravity loss.
questions.answer:
Ideal rocket speed gain:
\[
\Delta v_{\mathrm{ideal}}=2500\ln\left(\frac{1200}{800}\right)=1014\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Gravity loss over \(20\,\mathrm{s}\):
\[
gt=9.8(20)=196\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Burnout speed from rest:
\[
v=1014-196=818\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A rocket stage has \(v_e=3200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Derive and calculate the propellant mass fraction needed for \(\Delta v=2400\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), ignoring external forces.
questions.answer:
From the rocket equation,
\[
\frac{m_0}{m_f}=e^{\Delta v/v_e}
\]
The propellant fraction of the initial mass is
\[
f=1-\frac{m_f}{m_0}=1-e^{-\Delta v/v_e}
\]
For the given values,
\[
f=1-e^{-2400/3200}=0.528
\]
So about \(52.8\%\) of the initial mass must be propellant.

questions.prompt: A vertical rocket starts from rest with \(m_0=900\,\mathrm{kg}\), burns to \(m_f=600\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(15\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}\), and has \(v_e=2200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Ignoring drag, find the burnout speed and check whether it initially lifts off. State assumptions.
questions.answer:
Assume vertical motion, constant \(g\), constant exhaust speed, constant mass flow, and no drag. The burn time is
\[
t_b=\frac{900-600}{15}=20\,\mathrm{s}
\]
The burnout speed is
\[
v_b=2200\ln\left(\frac{900}{600}\right)-9.8(20)
\]
\[
v_b=696\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Initial thrust is
\[
T=\alpha v_e=15(2200)=33000\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Initial weight is
\[
mg=900(9.8)=8820\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Since thrust exceeds initial weight, it initially lifts off. The interpretation is that acceleration increases as mass falls.

questions.prompt: For a vertical rocket with constant exhaust speed \(v_e\), constant mass flow rate \(\alpha\), initial mass \(m_0\), final mass \(m_f\), and uniform gravity \(g\), derive the burnout speed from rest and the condition for positive upward acceleration throughout the burn. State assumptions and interpret the condition.
questions.answer:
Assume vertical motion, no drag, constant \(g\), constant \(v_e\), and constant mass flow rate \(\alpha=-dm/dt>0\). Burn time is
\[
t_b=\frac{m_0-m_f}{\alpha}
\]
The velocity equation is
\[
dv=-v_e\frac{dm}{m}-g\,dt
\]
Integrating from \(m_0\) to \(m_f\):
\[
v_b=v_e\ln\left(\frac{m_0}{m_f}\right)-g\frac{m_0-m_f}{\alpha}
\]
Instantaneous acceleration is
\[
a(t)=\frac{\alpha v_e}{m(t)}-g
\]
This is smallest at the initial mass \(m_0\), so positive upward acceleration throughout requires
\[
\frac{\alpha v_e}{m_0}>g
\]
Interpretation: initial thrust must exceed initial weight; after that, decreasing mass makes the condition easier to satisfy.
